workflow.title: Typical workflow

firstRun.title: First run
firstRun.body: When pi starts in a new project and a hub is configured, kankaku asks for the client and project (with a skip option). Answering "yes" to "remember for this repository?" saves the choice in "KANKAKU_DIR/config.json", so it won't ask again.

dailyUse.title: Daily use
dailyUse.body: kankaku syncs on its own, without ever blocking a prompt: on session start and after each agent turn, throttled to at most once every 5 minutes ("KANKAKU_SYNC_MIN_INTERVAL_MINUTES"). New entries show up in this hub's dashboard without you doing anything.

reassigning.title: Reassigning history
reassigning.body: Run "/kankaku backfill" to force a full sync and see how many old tasks landed in "Sin determinar". Reassign them from this web app's unassigned queue.

workflow.keyRule: Key rule: once you reassign a task in this web app, a later kankaku sync never undoes that reassignment — it only updates measurement fields (time, cost, status), never client or project.

config.title: Configuration

env.dir: Directory for the work log (`worklog.jsonl`) and crash-recovery checkpoints, relative to the project cwd unless given as an absolute path.
env.interactiveTools: Comma-separated list of tool names whose execution span counts as waiting time.
env.segments: ";"-separated "tag=tool:regex" rules for tagged segments (defaults to the single "review" rule).
env.client: Default billing client for this project; lower precedence than "/kankaku client", higher than the project's "config.json".
env.pbUrl: PocketBase hub URL. Must be HTTPS unless it points at localhost/127.0.0.1/::1.
env.machine: This machine's display name, attached to every record as "machine" once the hub is configured.
env.syncPrompt: Prompt privacy for sync: "none" (omitted), "truncated" (first 120 characters), or "full".
env.syncWindowHours: How many hours behind the sync watermark are re-evaluated on every run, to catch subagents that settle late.
env.syncRecords: "0" disables uploading "work_records" (raw detail); "task_entries" are always uploaded.
env.syncAuto: "0" disables the automatic "session_start"/"agent_settled" sync; "/kankaku sync" still works.
env.syncMinInterval: Minimum minutes between automatic syncs; "0" disables the throttle. Never applies to a manual sync.

config.credentialsBody: Instead of environment variables, kankaku also reads "~/.kankaku/credentials.json" (recommended "chmod 600"). Environment variables take precedence, field by field, over this file.
config.connectBody: Copy and run this in the terminal where you use pi, replacing the password with the real service account's — never the owner account — ask whoever administers this hub for it.
config.loadInPiTitle: Load this branch's build in pi
config.loadInPiBody: To try this build without publishing or installing it:
config.loadInPiNote: If the published version is already installed (pi install npm:kankaku), uninstall it first: otherwise kankaku loads twice and every prompt is recorded in duplicate. With -e the extension does not reach subagents; for that, install the local checkout with pi install and its absolute path.
config.serviceAccountNote: Always use the service account ("role: \"service\""), never the owner account — it's the only one allowed to write "task_entries"/"work_records".

summary-today.description: Shows today's totals (work, waiting, record count) by role, plus a union-based tasks segment, each with its estimated cost.
summary-today.whenToUse: To see at a glance how much you've worked today and its cost, without leaving pi.

summary-all.description: Same as "/kankaku", but across every historical record instead of just today's.
summary-all.whenToUse: To see the full accumulated total, e.g. when reviewing overall usage.

tasks.description: One line per task (time, union of work/waiting, cost, subagent count, truncated prompt) for the current pi session.
tasks.whenToUse: To review which tasks ran in the current session and what they cost.

tasks-all.description: Same as "tasks", but across every session instead of only the current one.
tasks-all.whenToUse: To review the full task history, not just this session's.

sessions.description: One line per session today (id, time range, union of work/waiting, cost, task count).
sessions.whenToUse: To see how many pi sessions you've had today and their combined cost.

sessions-all.description: Same as "sessions", but across every day instead of only today.
sessions-all.whenToUse: For a historical review of every recorded session.

clients.description: Today's totals (work, waiting, wall time, cost, task count) grouped by billing client. Tasks with no resolved client are grouped under "(none)".
clients.whenToUse: To see where today's time went by client, with or without a hub configured.

clients-all.description: Same as "clients", but summed across every day.
clients-all.whenToUse: For the full historical breakdown by client.

projects.description: Today's totals by project, same shape as "clients" but grouped by project. Only available with a hub configured.
projects.whenToUse: To see where today's time went by project.

projects-all.description: Same as "projects", but summed across every day.
projects-all.whenToUse: For the full historical breakdown by project.

client-show.description: Shows the effective billing client for the current session and which source it came from (session, "KANKAKU_CLIENT", or the project's "config.json").
client-show.whenToUse: To check which client is being applied before kankaku records more work.

client-set.description: Sets the billing client for the current session. With a hub configured, the name must match a catalog client's code or name (case-insensitive) and also sets the target with no project.
client-set.whenToUse: To fix or force a session's client before work gets recorded under the wrong one.

client-clear.description: Clears the session-level client override, so resolution falls back to the next source in precedence.
client-clear.whenToUse: To undo a client set earlier in this session with "/kankaku client".

target-show.description: Shows the effective hub target (client + project) and which source it came from: session, project "config.json", "repo_paths", or the picker. Hub-only.
target-show.whenToUse: To check which client and project work is being attributed to before syncing.

target-pick.description: Re-runs the client/project picker even if one is already resolved. The new target applies to records settled after this command.
target-pick.whenToUse: To switch client or project mid-session without restarting pi.

target-clear.description: Clears the session-level target, so resolution falls back to "config.json", "repo_paths", or the picker.
target-clear.whenToUse: To undo a "/kankaku target pick" set earlier in this session.

catalog-refresh.description: Forces a catalog (clients/projects) refresh from the hub instead of waiting for the 6-hour cache to expire, and reports how many clients/projects came back.
catalog-refresh.whenToUse: After creating or editing a client or project in this web app, so kankaku sees it right away.

sync.description: Pushes pending tasks to the hub: new ones, plus anything inside the revisit window ("KANKAKU_SYNC_WINDOW_HOURS", 24h by default) that changed.
sync.whenToUse: To force a manual sync instead of waiting for the automatic one after each prompt.

sync-all.description: A full re-evaluation: revisits every task, not just the recent window. The content hash keeps it cheap even when nothing changed.
sync-all.whenToUse: When you suspect something didn't reach the hub, or after changing sync configuration.

sync-status.description: Shows the sync watermark ("syncedThrough"), a locally-computed pending count (no network call), and the last sync error, if any.
sync-status.whenToUse: To check whether automatic sync is up to date without triggering one.

backfill.description: Runs a full sync and reports the result grouped by the old free-text label ("legacy_client_label"): how many tasks went to "Sin determinar" and under which name.
backfill.whenToUse: The first time you connect a historical project to the hub, to know what to reassign afterwards in the unassigned queue.

export.description: Writes one row per task (today's by default, or every task with "all") as CSV or JSON, under "KANKAKU_DIR/export/".
export.whenToUse: To take the data outside pi, e.g. into a spreadsheet.
